title: A closed immersion into projective space supplies an ample invertible sheaf
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be a morphism, and suppose that for some $n$ there is a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_A$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], where $\mathbf P^n_A$ is the base change of projective space [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Let $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_A}(1)$ be the standard twisting sheaf [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Then $\mathcal L=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_A}(1)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] that is $f$-ample [def-sc-ample]. Here $f$-ample means relatively ample in the sense of Stacks Tags 01PS (definition-ample) and 01VG (definition-relatively-ample): some positive tensor power is relatively very ample, i.e. gives a closed immersion over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ into a projective space.

lead_note: L (2026-10-10): the citation of def-sc-ample (ample over a field) does not fit a scheme over Spec A; the absolute notion is def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module (Stacks 01PS), and over an affine base f-ample is the same as ample (01VK). The splitter of this node should restate ampleness through that node so that lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation applies.
